questions.question: A client with possible dysphagia coughs and develops a wet voice after a sip of water. What should the RN do first?
choices: Offer a larger sip to confirm the finding
Stop oral intake, keep the client upright, and assess according to the swallowing-safety plan
Place the client flat to rest
Add a straw and ask the client to drink quickly
questions.explanation: Coughing and a wet voice after swallowing are concerning for impaired airway protection. Stop intake and maintain upright positioning while following the assessment and escalation plan.

questions.question: Which intervention most directly reduces heel pressure for an immobile client?
choices: Massage reddened heel tissue
Place a ring-shaped cushion under each heel
Float the heels so they are off the mattress
Keep the head of the bed at its highest position
questions.explanation: Offloading removes sustained pressure from the heels. Massaging injured tissue, ring devices, and unnecessary high head elevation can worsen tissue stress or shear.

questions.question: After administering an ordered opioid for acute pain, which follow-up is most important?
choices: Reassess pain, respiratory status, sedation, and function at the appropriate time
Wait until the end of the shift to avoid disturbing the client
Document only that the dose was given
Ask the next shift to decide whether the medication worked
questions.explanation: Evaluation includes both therapeutic effect and adverse effects, especially respiratory depression and sedation. Administration without timely reassessment is incomplete care.

questions.question: Before a first assisted walk after surgery, which finding requires assessment before standing?
choices: New lightheadedness while sitting at the bedside
A request to use the prescribed walker
A plan to wear nonslip footwear
A need for help managing IV tubing
questions.explanation: New positional symptoms suggest intolerance and fall risk. Assess and support the client before advancing activity; a walker, footwear, and tubing assistance are expected safety measures.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client cannot bear weight and needs a bed-to-chair transfer. Which plan is safest?
choices: Use the assessed mechanical-lift plan with trained staff
Ask one strong staff member to pivot the client
Use a gait belt so weight-bearing ability is unnecessary
Ask the client to hold the RN's neck during the transfer
questions.explanation: Match transfer equipment and staffing to the mobility assessment. A gait belt or staff strength does not make a non-weight-bearing pivot safe, and pulling on the caregiver risks injury.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: During assisted walking, a client becomes dizzy and their knees begin to buckle. What should the RN do?
choices: Stop, support the client safely to a seated or lying position, and assess with help
Continue slowly to avoid interrupting rehabilitation
Leave the client standing while retrieving a blood-pressure cuff
Ask the client to lean against the IV pole and rest
questions.explanation: Prevent a fall and assess the new symptoms. Finishing the walk is not the priority; leaving the client unsupported or relying on an IV pole adds risk.

questions.question: A stable client can wash their face and upper body but tires when reaching their legs. Which plan best supports function?
choices: Provide supplies and rest periods, and assist with areas the client cannot safely reach
Complete the entire bath for the client every day
Require the client to finish independently to build endurance
Delay all hygiene until the client can complete it without help
questions.explanation: Individualized assistance preserves ability and dignity without excessive exertion. Doing everything unnecessarily removes participation; insisting on full independence ignores the assessment.

questions.question: A client declines a scheduled bath, saying it hurts to turn. What is the best response?
choices: Explore pain and preferences, then agree on a safe comfort and hygiene plan
Document noncompliance and omit further discussion
Explain that scheduled bathing cannot be changed
Ask an assistant to bathe the client despite the refusal
questions.explanation: Explore the reason for refusal and address pain, timing, and alternatives with the client. A routine schedule does not override consent, and a label does not identify the care barrier.

questions.question: An incontinent client's skin is damp and irritated. Which action belongs in the initial care plan?
choices: Gently cleanse, dry, protect the skin, and reassess the continence plan
Scrub the area vigorously to remove all moisture
Apply a thick layer of powder to conceal redness
Restrict all oral fluids to prevent further incontinence
questions.explanation: Moisture management and individualized continence care reduce skin exposure to irritants. Scrubbing damages fragile tissue; concealing findings or broadly restricting fluids does not address the cause.

questions.question: Which finding best shows that an adapted daily-care plan is working?
choices: The client participates within tolerance, with manageable symptoms and intact skin
The bath is finished faster even though the client remains breathless
Staff complete every task without inviting client participation
The client stays in bed all day to avoid any discomfort
questions.explanation: Evaluate function, comfort, symptoms, and skin—not speed alone. Breathlessness needs reassessment; unnecessary dependence or immobility can create additional harm.
